title: Postiz: Extending Post-increment Addressing for Loop Optimization and Code Size Reduction
problem: Memory access instructions with auto-addressing modes exist in many ISAs but are underutilized by compilers. Existing optimization methods either focus narrowly on code size (basic-block level) or neglect post-increment instructions and outer loops.
motivation: Post-increment instructions reduce code size and improve performance on ML workloads; underutilization represents missed optimization opportunity especially for resource-constrained ML accelerators.
method: Postiz extends post-increment optimization beyond basic blocks to inner loops, cross-loop regions, and nested structures. Uses profitability analysis to optimize judiciously, balancing architectural benefits against other optimizations. Implements in LLVM for multiple ISA targets.
key_novelty: First compiler approach to systematically exploit post-increment instructions across loop hierarchies with cross-loop and nested loop support.
contributions: Post-increment optimization for inner loops, cross-loop regions, nested structures
98.04% optimization coverage on MobileNet and BERT
4× more post-increment instructions than default LLVM, 9.45% code size reduction

metrics.other: 9.45% average code size reduction, 4× post-increment instruction increase

limitations: Performance impact on execution time not detailed; hardware-specific cost modeling not discussed.
